why_useful: Could give a crude 'share of web indexed' time series by host, potentially proxying travel-site web presence/engagement trend over years, complementing our existing CDX/WARC captures.
size_hint: code only; pre-computed stats on S3 are modest CSVs per crawl
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Could give a crude 'share of web indexed' time series by host, potentially proxying travel-site web presence/engagement trend over years, complementing our existing CDX/WARC captures.

Gives a long, free, point-in-time-stamped (one file per monthly crawl, never revised) time series of overall web-crawl composition -- e.g., domain counts, HTTPS adoption, language mix -- useful as a macro internet-activity control variable, and the published files are themselves already a historical vintage register (each crawl's stats file is dated and never overwritten), which is exactly the kind of point-in-time discipline gap 4 wants, even though the subject is the whole web rather than ABNB-specific.

name: covid-19-open-data
what_it_holds: Google-maintained (now archived) open-data pipeline merging epidemiology, hospitalizations, vaccinations, and a dedicated Mobility table (Google Community Mobility metrics) across >20,000 locations at 4 aggregation levels (country/state/county/locality) as a daily time series through ~15-Sep-2022. Pipeline code (to re-run locally against sources) plus generated CSV outputs under CC BY; mobility subset still requires accepting Google's mobility-report ToS. Repo archived Nov 2024.
why_useful: Broader and better-structured than a raw Google Mobility CSV dump — includes county/locality-level granularity and is joinable to other macro/health covariates already in the same tables, useful for constructing a travel-demand recovery index by region (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) for historical base-rate work.
size_hint: Large multi-table daily panel, generated CSVs (data volume not fully inspected)
license: Apache-2.0 (code); CC BY (generated data); mobility subset under Google ToS
themes: Public-health and mobility indices: Google/Apple mobility archives, Cuebiq, SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey samples, Placer.ai-like foot traffic, mobility datasets by city
why_all: Broader and better-structured than a raw Google Mobility CSV dump — includes county/locality-level granularity and is joinable to other macro/health covariates already in the same tables, useful for constructing a travel-demand recovery index by region (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC) for historical base-rate work.

The authoritative, best-documented version of the same Google mobility signal as the ActiveConclusion mirror, with a clean harmonized geography key across country/state/county/locality that is far easier to join to other panels (e.g., Eurostat, TSA, FRED) than the raw report PDFs Google used to publish. Useful as a validated historical baseline for movement-vs-travel-demand relationships and as a schema template for any new mobility index construction.

name: 72m-domains-dataset
what_it_holds: 72,475,235 unique registered domains extracted via DuckDB from Common Crawl's cc-index columnar Parquet files, deduplicated across 14 monthly snapshots Jan 2025-Feb 2026. Stored as Parquet (built from an SQLite intermediate). 25 stars, license 'Other', updated 1 Sep 2026, actively maintained.
why_useful: A monthly-cadence global domain-presence list built directly from the cc-index columnar query pattern named in this theme; could be used to check month-by-month whether specific competitor/STR-adjacent domains (Vrbo, Hipcamp, Sonder, Tujia, Xiaozhu, AllTheRooms) are crawled/indexed at all, and shows exactly how to run the same cc-index Parquet query ourselves for a custom domain list or date range.
themes: Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
